subject: History
description: Classical Indian empires, kings, coins, culture

questions.stem: The Gupta empire's 'GOLDEN AGE' is typically associated with the reign of:
questions.explanation: Chandragupta II / Vikramaditya (r. ~380-415 CE) — conquered western Saka kingdoms, Gupta empire at peak extent. Navaratna court (including Kalidasa). Fa-Hien (Chinese pilgrim) visited India during his reign. Samudragupta was his father — also great conqueror ('Indian Napoleon').
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Samudragupta's achievements are documented in the:
questions.explanation: Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar) — composed by court poet Harisena — lists Samudragupta's military conquests in a 'dig-vijaya' style. Aihole inscription = Pulakesin II (Chalukya) by Ravikirti. Hathigumpha = Kharavela of Kalinga. Junagadh = Rudradaman I (Saka). Allahabad Pillar inscription by Harisena.
questions.subject: History

_fixes.was: Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription by Harisena)

questions.stem: KALIDASA, the great Sanskrit poet-playwright, lived during the reign of:
questions.explanation: Kalidasa — one of the 'Navaratnas' (nine jewels) of Chandragupta II's court. Major works: Abhijnanashakuntalam (play), Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava (poems), Vikramorvashiya, Malavikagnimitra (plays). Dated c. 4th-5th century CE.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Chola dynasty built the MAGNIFICENT BRIHADEESHWARA TEMPLE at Thanjavur. Its builder was:
questions.explanation: Raja Raja Chola I built Brihadeshwara (Peruvudaiyar Kovil) in 1010 CE — 1000th anniversary celebrated in 2010. Dedicated to Shiva. Main vimana is ~66 m tall. UNESCO WHS 1987 (part of 'Great Living Chola Temples'). His son Rajendra I built the Gangaikonda Cholapuram temple later. r. 985-1014 CE.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Rajendra Chola I (r. 1014-1044 CE) is remembered mainly for:

options.option_text: His naval expedition to Southeast Asia (Srivijaya)

questions.explanation: Rajendra Chola — launched a celebrated naval expedition c. 1025 CE against the Srivijaya empire (present Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand). Also conquered Bengal and Magadha. Built Gangaikonda Cholapuram ('city of the Chola who conquered the Ganges') as new capital.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The GUPTA empire was finally weakened (5th century CE) by invasions of the:
questions.explanation: Hun / Huna invasions from Central Asia started in the mid-5th century CE. Skandagupta (Kumaragupta's son) initially repelled them, but by early 6th century the Hunas under Toramana and Mihirakula had broken the empire's hold in north-west India.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: ARYABHATA, the mathematician-astronomer who worked out the value of π and the concept of zero, lived during:
questions.explanation: Aryabhata — born 476 CE. His magnum opus 'Aryabhatiya' (499 CE) covered arithmetic, algebra, trigonometry, and astronomy. Proposed heliocentric ideas (Earth rotates on its axis). India's first satellite (launched 1975) was named Aryabhata in his honour. Other Gupta-era intellectuals: Varahamihira, Brahmagupta (slightly later). 5th century CE.
